A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. Neither contains appendices: both end with references despite citing separate supplementary material. The supplied content supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 3 and 5 report original MMLU/MMMU attack evaluations, selection-strategy comparisons, ablations and runtime measurements in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and the qualitative attack example in Figure 3.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain the same FJ parameter recovery, fixed adversarial stances, selective influence perturbations, leader–follower optimization and integration with stealth-adapted attacks. Rewording and added attribution do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate MMLU and MMMU under the same multimodal discussion scenarios, including monitored and unmonitored attacks and stealth-oriented adaptations. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain MCA, MAD-Spear, their original selection strategies and Variants I–VI. SelfCheckGPT, RAGAs and G-Safeguard remain the monitoring methods; ablation and runtime comparators also match.

E3.justification: Sections 3 and 5 retain GPT-4o, adversarial-agent and target-edge budgets, discussion configurations, configuration averaging, all three evaluation metrics and p = 10^-3. No experimental protocol revision is reported.

E4.justification: Both contain the same three formulation ablations on MAD-Spear/MMMU in Table 6, runtime analysis in Table 7 and qualitative case in Figure 3. References to further supplementary analyses are also retained.

E5.justification: Both report averaged results without seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Uncertainty-reporting practices do not change.

E6.justification: Corresponding results in Tables 1–7 match, and Figure 3 is identical. For example, the proposed MAD-Spear strategy on MMMU with RAGAs retains 41.7% ΔAcc, 44.6% ΔAgradv and 6.1% detection; solver time remains 0.54 seconds.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and Theorem 1 retain the same mathematical content. Added inspiration citations do not revise the formulation or theorem; both versions refer proofs and derivations to supplementary material absent from the supplied PDFs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: identifying the discussion-monitored scenario, designing a tailored attack and demonstrating that monitoring alone does not eliminate adversarial risks.

C2.justification: The stealth–effectiveness tradeoff, explanation of accumulating small adversarial influences and interpretation of monitoring's insufficiency are unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: v2 adds 'Code is available here' with a repository hyperlink in the abstract; v1 has no code-access pointer. Other implementation, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds three references, numbered 21, 22 and 35, and explicitly acknowledges inspiration from Gionis et al. (2013) and Li et al. (2023) in Sections 4.2–4.3. Related work now connects single-LLM and multi-agent trustworthiness research, while retaining the overall positioning.

P1.justification: There are limited sentence rewrites in related work, the formulation explanation and ablation discussion, plus keywords and a corresponding-author note. Citations switch from author–year to numerical style; section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The entire document adopts a substantially narrower text block, redesigned front matter, running headers and different typography. Figures and tables are resized and relocated; Tables 3 and 7 become standalone displays, and Tables 4–5 occupy separate pages. All three figure artworks and seven tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The new code-access pointer improves reproducibility information, and explicit acknowledgment of prior opinion-dynamics work clarifies methodological attribution. These are limited benefits: the scientific method, results and supporting analyses remain unchanged, and the extensive reformatting adds no scientific evidence.
